title: A myriadminded man, Mr Best reminded. Coleridge called him myriadminded.
html_source:
Although the “myriadminded” man here is Shakespeare, the epithet could also be applied to Odysseus, whom Homer in the first lines of the Odyssey calls “the man of many turns [or minds].”

This episode abounds with allusions linking Odysseus to Shakespeare (and later to Bloom).
